teaser.text: Boeing builds the machines that carry people and freight, defend governments, and operate in space. It makes money not only when it hands over an aircraft or system, but also when it keeps that equipment working.

stock.title: Boeing stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Boeing stock forecast: scenarios for future shares, the operating recovery they require, cash generation and today’s valuation.
stock.opening: Boeing’s weighted forecast is $124.89 in October 2027 and reaches $238.29 in October 2029. It hinges on turning stable production into accepted deliveries and recurring cash generation before dilution arrives.
stock.closing: The full Boeing memo also explains Boeing’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Boeing’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is $124.89 in October 2027, a -33% return. It reaches $238.29 in October 2029, a +28% return. The bear case has 33% probability; the base case has 49%. The bull case has 18%. The bear path reaches $0.00 in October 2027 and $332.87 in October 2029.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Boeing, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base case assumes revenue approaches $125B and the final margin reaches 6%. The bull case requires $140B and an 8% margin. The bear case assumes a 1% loss before only a slow recovery. H1 2026 produced $604M of operating income on $46,777M of revenue, while 2025 adjusted operating income was $3,236M. Management’s targets of 52 737s per month by 2027 and $1B–$3B of 2026 free cash flow support recovery, but neither target is profit guidance.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Boeing really make?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, operating cash did not cover capital spending, so free cash flow remained negative. Subtracting stock pay produces a stricter measure because shares given to employees still impose an economic cost on existing shareholders.

blocks.heading: How does Boeing’s price compare with earnings and cash?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio compares a share price with annual earnings per share. Boeing’s trailing and forward P/E ratios are both high, but the forward measure is a forecast, not profit already earned. The problem is that Boeing’s 2025 core earnings included a $12.47-per-share gain from selling Digital Aviation Solutions. Removing an exceptional gain can clarify repeatable profit, but it cannot remove the real costs of delays, rework and troubled programs.

Free cash flow is operating cash left after capital spending. Boeing’s current free-cash-flow yields are negative, and its common dividend yield is zero, so shareholders receive no cash income while the company consumes cash. Management maintained a 2026 free-cash-flow outlook of $1–3 billion, while describing $10 billion annually as attainable without giving a firm date.

earnings.meta_description: Boeing's next results are expected on October 27, 2026, with guidance and key delivery and cash tests to watch.
earnings.opening: Boeing's next results are expected on October 27, 2026. Watch whether stable production turns accepted deliveries into repeatable cash after the Justice Department payment.
earnings.closing: The full memo also explains Boeing's business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to $1,000–$3,000 million of free cash flow in 2026 and $5,000–$7,000 million of operating cash flow. Capital spending is guided to $4,000 million. Delivery guidance calls for 500 737s and 90–100 787s in 2026. Production targets are 52 737s per month by 2027 and 10 787s per month by the end of 2026.

blocks.heading: Has Boeing kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Longer-term incentives can bite harder. Performance stock units tied to the 2023–2025 period paid zero because Boeing missed its free-cash-flow goals. A performance stock unit is a promise of shares that depends on specified results, so this was a real penalty. But Boeing’s certification promises also slipped: Ortberg hoped to complete certification of the 737-7 and 737-10 in 2025, while later expectations moved certification to 2026 and first deliveries to 2027.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in Boeing's next results?

paragraphs.text: Boeing’s third-quarter results on October 27 will show whether the company’s cash outlook survived the Justice Department payment. The useful comparison is among delivered aircraft, customer receipts and capital spending. A quarter helped by early customer payments can support the annual target without proving that the factory recovery is complete.

The 737 is the central production test. Boeing was building MAX aircraft at 47 a month, but the rate remained unstable. The 737-7 was certified while the 737-10 still awaited approval. Reaching 52 aircraft a month in 2027 requires steadier Renton operations and an approved, productive Everett line. Certification proves that an aircraft design meets regulatory requirements; it does not prove that the factory can build it reliably.
